On 30 October 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2704 (2023) [S/PV.9461, p. 2], based on the United Kingdom draft S/2023/808. The resolution extends the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. It expresses the Council's willingness to collaborate with the Colombian Government on further extensions, contingent upon agreement between the parties [OPERATIVE].

Regarding the Government–ELN ceasefire, Resolution 2694 previously established the Mission's monitoring and verification role [ADDITIONAL]. Resolution 2704 similarly expresses willingness to consider verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire, provided the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate protocols and updates on Resolution 2694 implementation [ADDITIONAL].

While Brazil emphasized Colombia's sovereign will and peace strategy, requesting authorization for EMC verification once mature [working_notes], the record clarifies that the resolution did not explicitly authorize this specific request [working_notes]. Ghana supported verification mechanisms in the EMC case, but only conditionally upon the Secretary-General's stipulations [working_notes]. The Council's shared position affirms the extension of the current mandate and the conditional openness to future verification protocols, pending specific confirmations

On 30 October 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2704 (2023) via UK draft S/2023/808 [S/PV.9461, p. 2]. The resolution extends the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. It expresses the Council's willingness to collaborate with the Colombian Government on further mandate extensions based on inter-party agreement [OPERATIVE].

Regarding the Government–EMC ceasefire, the Council expressed willingness to consider monitoring and verification protocols contingent upon the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire and updating on Resolution 2694 implementation [ADDITIONAL]. Brazil emphasized Colombia's sovereign will, requesting Council authorization for EMC verification once mature [working_notes]. Ghana, speaking for African members, welcomed the extension and supported EMC monitoring under Secretary-General conditions, pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous peoples [working_notes].

The Council preserved a shared position on extending the Mission's core mandate while maintaining flexibility for future ceasefire verification mechanisms dependent on verified ground realities and inter-party consensus. All 15 members voted in favour [working_notes].

On 30 May 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2682 (2023) [S/PV.9331, p. 2], extending the mandate of UNAMI to 31 May 2024. The resolution prioritizes inclusive political dialogue and reconciliation with full women's participation, formalizing the mission's operational framework under Council authority [Working Note 1].

Regarding reporting, the resolution does not mandate biannual submissions [Working Note 2]. Instead, it requires a single independent strategic review by the Secretary-General, due no later than 31 March 2024. This review must assess threats, mandate relevance, and staffing needs. Consultation is mandatory with Iraq, UN agencies, Member States, regional organizations, independent experts, civil society, and Kuwait [Working Note 2]. Iraq's government expressed support for this review in a letter dated 18 May 2023 [Working Note 2]. The authorized scope remains defined by the Council's authority, with no national explanations recorded for the vote [S/PV.9331, p. 2].

On 30 May 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2682 (2023) [S/PV.9331, p. 2], extending the mandate of UNAMI to 31 May 2024. The resolution prioritizes inclusive political dialogue and reconciliation, with a request to the Secretary-General to report biannually on the mission's fulfilment of responsibilities [Working Note 1]. This decision formalized the operational framework under Council authority, supported by Iraq's request [Working Note 1].

Additionally, the resolution mandates a strategic review of UNAMI by 31 March 2024. This review must assess threats, mandate relevance, structure, staffing, and regional cooperation support [Working Note 2]. The scope is defined in S/2023/378 [Working Note 2]. While working notes suggest a focus on full women's participation, the official record contains no specific requirements for this element, limiting verification of that mandate extension component [Working Note 2]. No national explanations of vote were recorded.
